title: CS2 World Bundle lane-geometry record (contract section 5B v2)
description: One line of lanemeshes.jsonl (JSON Lines): the parameters a consumer needs to bend the referenced prefab's straight part meshes (laneprefabs.json + lanemeshes/) along the lane's curve. The bend algorithm is normative in the contract and reference-implemented in tools/blender_import_bundle.py.

id.description: Producer-local stable identifier (the ECS entity index). Unique within the file.

category.description: Copy of the catalogue entry's category, for filtering without the join.

owner.description: The id of the owning edge, node or object where one exists - the same id space lanes.jsonl and instances.jsonl use.

curve.description: The lane's cubic bezier: four world-space control points in bundle-frame metres.

parts.description: Indices into the catalogue entry's parts array this lane draws - the game's per-lane sub-mesh selection, already resolved by the producer.

spans.description: Uncut curve-parameter ranges (CutRange holes: a driveway through a fence, a junction through a hedge). Absent means the whole curve [0, 1].

widthScale.description: Width scale at the curve's start and end (NodeLane.m_WidthOffset over the prefab width). Absent means [1, 1].

hang.description: HangingLane.m_Distances: the drop in metres at the curve's two ends. Present only for hanging lanes; the prefab-level sag factor is the catalogue entry's 'hanging'. The consumer builds the cubic (d0, (d0+h*L)*2/3, (d1+h*L)*2/3, d1) and subtracts it from world y at tGlobal.

tunnel.description: True when the owning network runs below ground - the game draws this lane on its Tunnel cutaway layer. The bundle ships tunnels fully rendered (the terrain cutout opens their portals); a consumer wanting only the surface world filters on this. Absent means surface.

colorSet.description: The lane's resolved paint - three linear RGBA channels, same shape and meaning as the instance attrs.colorSet (contract section 7.2). Hedges are the visible case.
